exposure: Structural readiness for PPH care (drugs, equipment, staff)
Process readiness for PPH care (knowledge, attitudes, and practices as related to WHO guidance on PPH care)
outcome: Availability of essential structural components needed to support key PPH processes of care
Level of process readiness for PPH care
cohort: The study included nine hospitals in Ghana and seven in Uganda, all of which had theoretical capacity for caesarean section and blood transfusion, along with maternity health service providers within these facilities.
finding: The study found generally good structural and process readiness for PPH care in Ghanaian and Ugandan referral-level facilities, but identified key gaps in specialist staffing, blood availability, and the utilization of tranexamic acid and uterine balloon tamponade.
cross-section timing: Current readiness at the time of the study
